title: Misalignment reports against the Synome Editor are open to anyone, with frivolity as the only filter
content:
A.1.3.2.4 pairs an unrestricted right with a discretionary filter: "Any party may report misalignment of the Synome Editor to Core GovOps. Core GovOps must review such reports, but may dismiss reports it determines to be frivolous, abusive, or made in bad faith."

The structure recurs throughout the Governance Scope — compare A.1.2.3.1, where community members may submit a Request for Review of Atlas document misalignment to the Core Facilitator, which "need not follow any specific template," with the Core Facilitator holding broad discretion in resolving it. In both cases the *submission* barrier is deliberately near zero and the *filtering* happens after intake, at the discretion of a named role.

The reasoning is asymmetric cost. A missed report of misalignment in an actor with unreviewed unilateral power is potentially catastrophic; a nuisance report costs a review. Formal templates and standing requirements would filter out noise but would also filter out the observer who noticed something real and cannot express it in procedural language — often exactly the person governance most needs to hear from.

What the pattern buys in accessibility it pays for in dependence on the gatekeeper. "Frivolous, abusive, or made in bad faith" is an unbounded standard applied by the same body that must otherwise act on the report, and dismissal is not visibly appealable here. The Atlas's own NR-1 flags this whole area — fact-finding, evidence handling, impartiality mechanisms — as unresolved research, which is the honest reading: the intake channel exists, the adjudication discipline behind it does not yet.
description: A.1.3.2.4 obliges Core GovOps to review any party's report but lets it dismiss those it deems frivolous, abusive, or in bad faith — a low-friction channel with a discretionary gate.
